question: What is the primary purpose of a stock card in a hospital ward?

options.A: Calculating the monthly salaries of nursing staff
options.B: Tracking the exact quantity of available supplies
options.C: Scheduling the daily cleaning duties for junior health workers
options.D: Recording patient vital signs over a twenty-four hour shift

explanation: Stock cards serve as a ledger to monitor inventory levels and movements of commodities within a clinical area. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is inventory control considered a core clinical responsibility for nurses?

options.A: It reduces the total number of admissions in the accident and emergency unit
options.B: It replaces the need for doctors to write official drug prescriptions
options.C: It ensures life-saving materials are available when patients need care
options.D: It completely eliminates the financial budget of the hospital administration

explanation: Nurses manage ward stores directly, meaning proper stock control guarantees that necessary clinical supplies are always on hand for patient emergencies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: What does the 'issues' column on a stock card represent?

options.A: Newly delivered supplies arriving from the central medical store
options.B: Damaged items returned directly to the manufacturing pharmaceutical company
options.C: The financial cost of purchasing a single unit of the drug
options.D: Quantities of stock taken out of the store for use

explanation: The issue section tracks items removed from inventory to be used in patient care or clinical procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: A nurse records newly delivered malaria medications in which section of the stock card?
explanation: Any incoming stock entering the ward inventory is logged under receipts to increase the overall available balance. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: What does reaching the reorder level on a stock card indicate?

options.A: It is time to submit a new requisition for supplies
options.B: The maximum storage capacity of the pharmacy has been exceeded
options.C: No more patients can be admitted to the clinical unit
options.D: All items in the ward store have officially expired

explanation: The reorder level acts as a trigger point telling the nurse to place a new order before inventory runs out. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: Why is keeping inventory below the maximum stock level important?

options.A: It prevents tied-up capital and reduces the risk of drug expiration
options.B: It allows nurses to spend more time on bedside patient documentation
options.C: It guarantees that central medical stores will deliver supplies instantly
options.D: It completely stops the need for keeping physical stock card ledgers

explanation: Overstocking leads to wastage through expired medications and wastes financial resources that could be used elsewhere. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: When should a nurse update the stock card after issuing items to a ward?

options.A: Whenever the ward runs completely out of supplies
options.B: Only when the central store supervisor visits
options.D: At the end of every working month

explanation: Immediate recording prevents errors and ensures that the stock balance is always accurate and up to date. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: A nurse counts 10 ampoules of oxytocin on the shelf, but the stock card balance reads 15. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Order fifty more ampoules from the pharmacy to replace the missing stock
options.B: Investigate the discrepancy immediately to find the missing items
options.C: Ignore the difference since five ampoules is a very small number
options.D: Cross out the stock card and write down a completely new maximum level

explanation: Unexplained differences between physical stock and ledger balances require immediate investigation to identify errors, loss, or theft. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is lead time in the context of ordering medical commodities?

options.A: The shelf life of a drug before its official expiration date
options.B: The time between placing an order and receiving the items
options.C: The duration a patient spends admitted in the emergency ward
options.D: The total number of hours a nurse spends filling out stock ledgers

explanation: Lead time measures the delay interval from when a requisition is submitted until the supplies actually arrive on the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why does a longer delivery lead time require a higher reorder level?

options.A: To prevent stockouts while waiting for delayed shipments to arrive
options.B: To force nurses to perform physical stock counts twice every shift
options.C: To increase the total financial cost of the hospital procurement budget
options.D: To reduce the storage space required in the main hospital pharmacy

explanation: When delivery takes longer, inventory will deplete further before new supplies arrive, requiring a higher threshold to bridge the gap. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which action should be taken FIRST when a new supply of drugs is delivered to the ward?

options.A: Sign the delivery note without opening the boxes to save time
options.B: Discard the old stock card and start a fresh inventory ledger
options.C: Inspect the items for quantity accuracy, damage, and expiration dates
options.D: Store the items immediately in the back of the ward cupboard

explanation: Incoming deliveries must be inspected first to verify that the correct quantity, quality, and usable expiry dates have arrived. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: A nurse receives a carton of intravenous fluids where half of the bags have broken seals. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Record the full carton in the receipts column of the stock card anyway
options.B: Reject the damaged items and document the discrepancy on the delivery note
options.C: Hide the damaged fluids in the utility room until the next inspection
options.D: Accept the entire carton and issue the damaged bags to patients quickly

explanation: Compromised or damaged supplies are unsafe for patient use and should be rejected or reported immediately rather than entered into usable inventory. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: What does the FEFO inventory management principle stand for?
explanation: The FEFO principle ensures that commodities closer to their expiration date are dispensed before newer shipments to prevent wastage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct result of poor inventory management on a hospital ward?

options.A: Increased availability of life-saving drugs during emergency shifts
options.B: Unexplained discrepancies between physical counts and ledger balances
options.C: High quantities of expired medicines wasting valuable storage space
options.D: Sudden stockouts halting routine surgical and nursing procedures

explanation: Poor inventory management causes shortages and stockouts, not increased availability of necessary medications. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h7)
